title: Quantum computing - Wikipedia
snippet: Quantum computing is a type of computation that harnesses the collective properties of quantum states, such as superposition, interference, and entanglement, to perform calculations.

title: What is Quantum Computing? - IBM
snippet: Quantum computers use qubits to operate in more than one state (0 and 1 at the same time) and can solve certain problems much faster than classical computers, such as factoring large numbers.

title: Quantum Computing Overview - Google Quantum AI
snippet: Quantum computing could dramatically accelerate tasks like drug discovery, materials science, cryptography and optimization. Google demonstrated quantum supremacy in 2019 with the Sycamore processor.

title: Qubit - an elementary unit of quantum information
snippet: A qubit is the basic unit of quantum information, a two-state quantum-mechanical system. Unlike a classical bit, a qubit can exist in a superposition of both states.

title: Quantum error correction explained - Nature
snippet: Error correction is the central challenge of quantum computing. Logical qubits built from many physical qubits can correct errors, but require thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit today.

title: Quantum supremacy - Google 2019 experiment
snippet: Google's Sycamore processor performed a task in 200 seconds that would take a classical supercomputer 10,000 years, demonstrating quantum supremacy for the first time.

title: Shor's algorithm - integer factorization
snippet: Shor's algorithm is a quantum algorithm that factors integers in polynomial time, threatening RSA cryptography if large-scale quantum computers become available.

title: Quantum supremacy - Wikipedia
snippet: Quantum supremacy marks the point at which a quantum computer can perform a computation that no classical computer can perform in a feasible amount of time.

title: Post-quantum cryptography - NIST
snippet: NIST has standardized post-quantum cryptographic algorithms designed to be secure against both quantum and classical computers, protecting against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks.

title: Superconducting qubits and cooling - ScienceDaily
snippet: Most quantum computers use superconducting qubits cooled to temperatures near absolute zero, inside dilution refrigerators, to maintain quantum coherence.

title: Artificial intelligence - Wikipedia
snippet: Artificial intelligence is intelligence demonstrated by machines, in contrast to the natural intelligence displayed by humans and animals. AI research has become a core part of technology.

title: Large language models explained - OpenAI
snippet: Large language models are trained on massive text corpora using next-token prediction, and can perform tasks ranging from code generation to summarization and dialogue.

title: Machine learning - Stanford CS229
snippet: Machine learning gives computers the ability to learn without being explicitly programmed, using techniques like supervised learning, unsupervised learning and reinforcement learning.

title: CRISPR gene editing overview - MIT
snippet: CRISPR is a gene-editing tool that allows scientists to alter DNA sequences and modify gene function, with applications in medicine, agriculture and biology research.

title: James Webb Space Telescope discoveries
snippet: The James Webb Space Telescope observes the universe in infrared, revealing galaxies from the early universe, exoplanet atmospheres and star formation regions.
